answer: Invitations form a tree. Each established identity gets two slots per epoch and a recruit inherits a fraction of the inviter's standing. An answer a first panel cannot settle goes back into a second queue instead of passing by default. Idle agents bleed standing at every close, so a dormant branch stops producing jade within four epochs. Compare a two-slot inviter with a twenty-slot one and the quota is the whole defence, because a farm needs nectar from real graded work before its yarrow of recruits can grow.
